Camera media commands in the WhatsApp bot

Camera media commands in the WhatsApp bot#

Add commands in WhatsApp Bot Builder, select the actions below, and save. Existing command settings are preserved; these commands are not enabled automatically.

Suggested trigger

Action

Example

/live

Get live streaming link (admin)

/live CAM-GATE-01

/snapgroup

Latest snapshots by camera group

/snapgroup Site A

/snaplocation

Latest snapshots by location

/snaplocation North Yard

Select a valid B-Snap API token in the builder. Both the token owner’s group and invoking whitelist number’s group apply. An unset group means no group restriction for that identity. Camera access uses the many-to-many memberships. Group/location names match the full name, case-insensitively, including spaces; SQL wildcard characters are treated literally. The live command accepts an exact hostname, camera UUID, or IP address.

Live links#

Set Configuration → General → Public B-Snap URL (app_public_url) to the browser-accessible B-Snap address. When empty, live links use PUBLIC_ORIGIN if configured. Missing/invalid URL settings return HTTP 409 with configuration instructions; token/access/not-found errors preserve their HTTP status instead of becoming a generic 502. Enable Maps Live View, and use an admin API token and whitelist admin sender to create a link. The returned link is public: its recipient needs no B-Snap login. It contains a signed grant for one camera, with no camera credentials or API token. Anyone holding that link can view the selected camera until the grant expires.

Links expire five minutes after creation. The API accepts expires_in between 30 and 900 seconds; the native bot action uses 300 seconds. The API response includes expires_at in UTC and requires_login: false. Generate a new link with the command after expiry. Tampered, expired, and cross-camera grants are rejected before camera I/O. Deleting the issuing user/whitelist entry, removing its admin role or camera-group access, changing camera status, or disabling Maps Live View revokes access. Ongoing viewers recheck these permissions, and playback is bounded by the remaining grant lifetime.

The public viewer shares the bounded Maps Live implementation. The original Maps Live endpoint still requires admin login. RTSP, ONVIF discovery, and HLS use FFmpeg; the link API itself does not probe cameras. An HTTP(S) snapshot URL instead refreshes its image every two seconds, supports Basic/Digest authentication, and works without an IP field. This is periodic image refresh; its motion rate depends on the snapshot endpoint. It does not create saved snapshots. HTTP snapshot redirects are rejected. Multipart MJPEG URLs are not single-image snapshot endpoints; use an RTSP/HLS source for video.

Streams retain the existing viewer capacity and three-minute duration limits; public and authenticated viewers share the issuing user’s capacity limit. Reopen an unexpired link to start another preview. No preview can extend the grant’s expiry, including when source resolution takes time. Camera status must be Active or Standalone. Missing/unreachable sources return a safe error when opened. Public responses disable caching and referrer forwarding. Application logs, audit events, and the WhatsApp message monitor do not retain the signed grant; reverse-proxy access logs should redact its token query parameter as well.

Default response template:

{{steps.result.body.camera}}
{{steps.result.body.url}}
Expires: {{steps.result.body.expires_at|datetime}}

Latest saved snapshots#

One command sends one latest non-deleted saved snapshot per accessible camera, including offline cameras. It does not capture new images. The bot automatically requests all API pages (50 cameras per page), so it is not limited to the five images used by the legacy hostname-prefix command. Large selections generate multiple WhatsApp image messages. Existing chat routing, quoted replies, HD delivery, audit preparation, and message-delivery monitoring are reused.

Cameras without a saved image, or whose latest file is missing, are reported in a text message. Deleted snapshots are excluded. Files outside the snapshot root are rejected. A missing latest file does not silently substitute an older image. Failure after preparing some images sends those images with a partial-failure notice. Transport failures use the existing media delivery failure notification.

The response template is rendered separately for each snapshot. Use response type Text; the native action attaches the images automatically. Timestamp formatting uses the configured timezone, including its timezone label. Execute Action previews show each prepared image with its configured caption, alongside missing-image notices. They never send WhatsApp messages or expose local filesystem paths.

Array-mapper templates also work: each image renders the loop against its own single-item steps.result.body.results, so other cameras do not appear in its caption. @index1 numbers images across API pages. Sample previews use the same per-image context; direct fields such as {{camera}} and {{steps.result.body.camera}} remain supported.

{{#each steps.result.body.results}}
{{@index1}}. {{this.camera}} | {{this.timestamp|datetime}}
{{/each}}

{{steps.result.body.camera}}
{{steps.result.body.timestamp|datetime}}

APIs#

  • GET /api/bot/cameras/live-link?keyword=CAM-GATE-01&phone_number=... requires admin authentication and an admin whitelist entry. Returns camera_id, camera, url, requires_login: false, expires_in, and expires_at. The returned /public/cameras/{camera_id}/live?token=... URL needs only its valid signed grant and does not accept an arbitrary camera source URL.

  • GET /api/bot/cameras/latest-snapshots?scope=group&keyword=Site%20A&phone_number=... accepts authenticated viewer/operator/admin users and whitelisted senders. Use scope=location for location filtering. page starts at 1; per_page is 1–50. Returns results, missing, total_cameras, page, and has_more. Each result includes camera_id, camera, snapshot_id, an ISO timestamp with UTC offset, and a protected snapshot url.

Both APIs require authentication even when a valid phone number is supplied. Protected snapshot URLs retain their normal authentication and group checks. Use the native actions for multi-image delivery; a generic API Flow image response still represents a single selected image.
